extracted.intended_audience: tenured mathematics faculty at U.S. or Canadian colleges and universities seeking a yearlong sabbatical-extension fellowship
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and evaluation criteria for applying to the Simons Fellows in Mathematics program (year‑long sabbatical salary‑replacement awards). Covers eligibility, allowable costs, application components, formatting and submission rules, and basis for award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards will be based on the applicant’s scientific accomplishments in the five-year period preceding the application and on the potential scientific impact of the work to be done during the leave period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers will consider recent (past five years) productivity and the anticipated impact of proposed sabbatical research; keywords selected by applicant will be used to choose suitable reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — sabbatical or equivalent leave‑eligible faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility is restricted to sabbatical or equivalent leave‑eligible faculty who wish to use the Simons Fellowship award for the purpose of extending at least a single-term sabbatical research leave to a full academic year without teaching or administrative responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A research leave provided by a unit of a university, rather than university-level sabbatical, would not normally be considered as sabbatical equivalent — contact the program for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — tenure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Simons Fellow in Mathematics must have a teaching or administrative tenured position at the same U.S. or Canadian college or university within the mathematics department at the time of application, throughout the course of the sabbatical research leave and in the term following the leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This must be the applicant’s primary position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — primary appointment in mathematics department
rubrics_metrics.description: Applied mathematics and statistics disciplines are eligible as long as the applicant resides within the mathematics, and not statistics, department. Those doing primarily mathematical education research are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants whose primary appointment is in another department (e.g., computer science) are not eligible even if their research is mathematical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot extend an already full-year sabbatical
rubrics_metrics.description: The fellowship program will not support the extension of a full year of sabbatical research leave to an additional term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship must be used to extend at least a single-term sabbatical to a full academic year, not to add time to an already full year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sabbatical length and institutional salary support requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To receive the fellowship, you must be approved by your institution for a full year of sabbatical research leave, consisting of two consecutive semesters or three consecutive quarters with at least 50 percent of the year fully paid by the home university and no more than 50 percent fully or partly supported by the fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If other resources are needed because foundation funds are insufficient, the foundation will consider mixed funding arrangements (e.g., university covers 80% and fellowship covers 20%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of sabbatical approval timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of sabbatical approval is not required at the time of application but must be provided to the foundation at least three months prior to the start of the applicant’s award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 'How to Apply' for required attachments and timing; host confirmation letters (if applicable) must also be provided at least three months prior to start.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and salary replacement limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides salary replacement for up to 50 percent (up to a maximum of $125,000) of the Fellow’s current academic‑year salary, inclusive of salary and fringe benefits, and up to an additional $10,000 for expenses related to the leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum total budget request should not exceed $162,000 USD. Fellowship funds are calculated relative to the academic‑year salary whether paid over 9, 10 or 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overhead / indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fellow’s home institution will receive an additional 20 percent overhead on allowable direct cost expenditures, per the foundation’s indirect cost policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include applicable institutional overhead in the budget; follow foundation indirect cost policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship period and contiguity
rubrics_metrics.description: The Simons Fellowship will fund up to 50 percent of the 2026–2027 academic year (examples: Jan 1–Dec 31, 2026; Sept 1, 2026–Aug 31, 2027; Jan 1–Dec 31, 2027). Fellowship funding must be contiguous to the university‑supported portion of the leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowship awards and sabbatical periods may begin no earlier than Jan 1, 2026 and no later than Jan 1, 2027; for sabbaticals beginning Jan 1, 2026 awards will be retroactively started and funds available no sooner than March 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of salary replacement funds — restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary replacement funds are to be used only to replace or partly replace salary during academic terms in which the recipient would otherwise be teaching or engaging in academic administration or other departmental or university committee work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding may not be used for summer salary (if salary is paid over nine months) or to increase the academic‑year salary beyond the university rate, but may be paid out over the full leave period. Follow university policy on sabbatical costs not supported by the university.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable leave‑related expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The additional funding (up to $10,000) is to be used to support expenses related to the leave in a manner consistent with the approved sabbatical plans. Allowable leave‑related expenses include small equipment and supplies, travel (including the Fellow and family members to and from the sabbatical location(s) and the Fellow’s travel to meetings and collaborators), housing (for the Fellow and family), automobile rental, childcare and support for visitors (including meals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salaries for students or research associates will not be supported, but funds may be used to help transport members of the Fellow’s research group to the sabbatical location and provide housing. Leave‑related expenses may be incurred at any time during the award period; not restricted to salary terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unspent funds and no-cost extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Unspent funds at the end of the grant must be returned to the foundation. No-cost extension requests will typically not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budget and spending accordingly; returning unspent funds is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation expects to award up to 50 mathematics fellowships for 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informational—sets applicant expectations about program scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simons Foundation / Flatiron employment restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Simons Foundation employees who receive a W‑2 from the Simons Foundation, including employees of the Flatiron Institute, may not apply as a PI to any Simons Foundation or Simons Foundation International RFAs released by the Simons Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs and any project personnel listed who will receive funding for salary, travel, support for students/postdocs/research staff, lab equipment, computing time or other individual expenses may not be employees of the Simons Foundation/Flatiron Institute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent awards and matching rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Simons Fellowship cannot be used to match another external fellowship. The foundation allows holding other awards (example: Travel Support Gift Award) simultaneously with a Simons Fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check program rules on simultaneous awards; you may hold certain other foundation awards concurrently but not use the fellowship as a match.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and citizenship eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. or Canadian citizenship is not required, but a grantee’s primary appointment must be at a U.S. or Canadian institution in order to apply to or hold the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary institutional appointment location is decisive for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emeriti, retired, adjunct appointment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Retired and emeriti faculty are not eligible. An adjunct faculty member whose primary employer is an academic institution and who is eligible on the basis of his or her research is eligible; a scientist whose primary appointment is at a national laboratory or research institute but who has an adjunct appointment is not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is determined by primary employer and level of teaching commitments/source of salary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission method and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit via the Simons Award Manager (SAM). The deadline is October 1, 2025, 12 p.m. (noon) EDT. Late applications will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your own SAM account; if new to SAM register first; ProposalCentral users should reset their SAM password. Create Application → Begin Application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal attachment formatting constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal attachments should be single spaced and in a common typeface and font size no smaller than 10 points. Margins must be at least half an inch in all directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to these formatting constraints or attachments risk being noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required proposal components and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement of Recent Work (two‑page limit, plus up to one page for references and figures); Statement of Sabbatical Plans (two‑page limit, plus up to one page for references and figures); Applicant Biosketch (SciENcv or fillable PDF NIH/NSF‑style); Students List; Letter from Other Institution (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements should explain recent significant work and summarize plans for the entire leave period, host institutions and main goals; follow specified page limits and attachment types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter from other institution requirements / backup plan
rubrics_metrics.description: If the leave is to be taken at another institution and will last longer than one month, confirmation must be submitted from the host institution(s) in the form of a letter signed by relevant department chairs or appropriate authorities describing approval and available facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the letter cannot be obtained, include a backup plan describing what would be done if visits were not possible; host location must be confirmed to the foundation at least three months prior to the award start. Use specified attachment type if including a backup plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget tab details and required justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Add a detailed, one‑year budget in U.S. dollars. In Personnel Costs, provide the applicant’s known or expected academic‑year salary for the full year as the Base Salary. Requested Salary and Fringe Cost should reflect the amount that will be covered by the Fellowship. For Leave Related Expenses, provide a brief itemization and justification not exceeding $10,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If salary is not finalized, note this in the justification column and include expected date of salary increase. An insufficient budget justification may result in the proposal not being considered further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications & Other Support requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications: list up to five accepted or published papers from the previous five years. Other Support: provide current and pending external PI or co‑PI support (all financial resources directly supporting the applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using SAM profile, select Other Support from Profile and assign to proposal. Reporting overlap is required to submit (select Yes/No for each entry). Overlap is not a consideration for funding in this program, but must be reported. If using PDF upload, NSF format is sufficient and should include award number, source, title, dates and total costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keywords selection for reviewer assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Select up to two tags (keywords) as it applies to the applicant’s research in the last five years. These choices will be used to select the most suitable reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose keywords carefully to ensure appropriate reviewer matching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of generative AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the extent to which, if any, generative AI technology was used and how it was used to develop your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be transparent about AI assistance in proposal preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Simons Foundation / Flatiron affiliations
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the PI or any project personnel listed on the application are affiliated with the Simons Foundation or the Flatiron Institute as a Visiting Scholar / Independent Contractor or Employee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note the prohibition on employees receiving a W‑2 applying as PI; disclose any affiliations for other personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application processing / institutional sign-off workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: When application complete, click 'Send for sign‑off' to send to your signing official for signature. The Signing Official must provide an electronic signature in the Submission tab. The applicant, Signing Official and Financial Officer will receive notifications when signed and submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will not be able to submit if the deadline has passed. Check Application Progress button to see any missing required information before sending for sign‑off.
